$comment: Every raw colour literal still living in frontend/src, mapped to the
semantic role it was serving. Two jobs:
1. EVIDENCE. The token layer claims to cover every role the 89 distinct
pre-token colours served. This is that claim, enumerated and tested:
tokens.contrast.test.js fails if a literal in frontend/src has no
entry here, or if an entry names a token that does not exist.
2. WORKLIST. The migration beads (collection, CardDetailView, sealed,
browse, the rest) read the replacement off this file instead of each
inventing its own. Where one literal served two roles, both are
listed and `note` says which goes where.
Entries are NOT pruned as migrations land — once frontend/src is clean
this file is the record of what became what, which is what a reviewer of
the last migration bead needs. Only unmapped literals fail the test.
Exact hex is preserved where it already passed AA; a `note` flags every
place the replacement is deliberately a different value.
MIGRATION COMPLETE (pd-eq99, 2026-08-03). frontend/src holds no literal
outside tokens.css, so job 2 — the worklist — is discharged and this file
is now purely job 1: the record. Where the last pass landed a literal
somewhere the earlier prediction did not anticipate, the entry below was
corrected to say where it ACTUALLY went, because a record that documents
an intention rather than an outcome is worse than none. Those corrections
are the ones carrying a `note` that names a call site.

#20243a.note: Also appears once as a border-bottom; that use becomes --color-border-subtle.

#0a0a1a.note: Used as a foreground once, over a bright collector-number badge — that is --color-text-inverse.

#43344a.note: The violet-tinted note callout in TcgExportModal; it was a one-off surface, not a role.

#0f3460.note: The identity rule. Its uses as a solid section-bar FILL became --color-info-surface; borders stayed --color-border. Two exceptions the migration found: the three hand-rolled set-completion meters in /browse, /browse/[set] and /browse/[set]/stats are progress TRACKS and took --color-progress-track (matching the ProgressBar primitive, and the pairing this manifest already declared for them); and /browse's group-header hover fill took --color-info-surface-hover, which is this exact value. Note --color-control-border is deliberately NOT this value — see tokens.css.

#6a7280.note: The Common bar in /browse/[set]/stats' rarity histogram. #3a3a52 (unknown rarity) is the one that took --color-chart-unknown; giving Common the same role would have erased the Common-vs-unknown distinction the histogram exists to show.

#fff.note: White on a crimson fill was 3.83:1 and is the single most common AA failure in the app. On --color-accent it becomes --color-on-accent (dark ink, 5.02:1); on --color-danger it stays white (4.79:1).

#c0d0f0.note: A ValueHistoryChart series, not body text.

#888.note: 134 uses, and 4.48:1 on the panel — one of the three documented AA failures. Replaced by --color-text-subtle at 6.10:1. Its single border-color use becomes --color-border-strong.

#e94560.note: 175 uses. As a FILL or BORDER it is unchanged (--color-accent / --color-border-accent, still exactly #e94560). As TEXT it was 4.46:1 on the page and 4.15:1 on the panel — both documented AA failures — so foreground uses become --color-text-accent (#ff6b85, 6.25/5.82).

#e7732f.note: The bundle-tile treatment in /browse. As the tile border it is --color-warning (a 3:1 non-text indicator); as the tile title and the `provisional` badge it is text, so --color-warning-text.

#f0c878.note: Warning text everywhere in CSS; its two chart-palette uses (PriceChart, the Illustration Rare bar) are --color-chart-3.

#ffd24a.note: Only ever the Hyper Rare bar in the rarity histogram — a categorical series, not warning text. Gold shifts to the lime step because --color-chart-3 (amber) is already spent on Illustration Rare.

#c0392b.note: Destructive actions move onto the --pd-red-* ramp so 'delete' stops reading as 'brand'.

#143b6d.note: Its only use was /browse's .grouphdr:hover. Collapsing it into --color-info-surface would have made the hover state identical to the rest state — the role exists so that affordance survives.

#2a5a8c.note: As a solid info FILL it was 2.22:1 against the panel; --color-info is lightened to #3877ac (3.33:1) and keeps white text at 4.77:1. As a chip border it is unchanged.

rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25).note: --shadow-sm is where it lives as a shadow. Its two uses as a BACKGROUND — the match picker's variant pip, the backup banner's inline <code> — are a wash that sinks a chip into whatever surface it sits on, which is --color-surface-shade.

rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.25).note: Marks the selected cell in the set-completion grid — that is a focus/selection indicator, not a white outline.
